title: pvTemporalShiftScale
body:
## pvTemporalShiftScale

Relabels time without touching the data: an input time t is reported as (t + PreShift) × Scale + PostShift, and a request for output time T fetches input time (T − PostShift) / Scale − PreShift. Use it to align runs that started at different times, change time units (Scale 0.001 turns milliseconds into seconds), or repeat a cyclic dataset with Periodic. Nothing is resampled; use pvTemporalInterpolator for in-between states.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The upstream description gives the transform as t*Shift + Scale; the native code applies PreShift before scaling and PostShift after it, so the two shifts differ by a factor of Scale.
- Keep Scale non-zero; the backward conversion divides by it.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `TemporalShiftScale`. Identity: `filters/TemporalShiftScale`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: The input to the Temporal Shift Scale filter. Accepted data: any data object (vtkDataObject). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":true,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataObject"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MaximumNumberOfPeriods` | If Periodic time is enabled, this controls how many time periods time is reported for. A filter cannot output an infinite number of time steps and therefore a finite number of periods is generated when reporting time. | `{"maximum":100.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |
| `Periodic` | If Periodic is true, requests for time will be wrapped around so that the source appears to be a periodic time source. If data exists for times {0,N-1}, setting periodic to true will cause time 0 to be produced when time N, 2N, 2N etc is requested. This effectively gives the source the ability to generate time data indefinitely in a loop. When combined with Shift/Scale, the time becomes periodic in the shifted and scaled time frame of reference. Note: Since the input time may not start at zero, the wrapping of time from the end of one period to the start of the next, will subtract the initial time - a source with T{5..6} repeated periodically will have output time {5..6..7..8} etc. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PeriodicEndCorrection` | If Periodic time is enabled, this flag determines if the last time step is the same as the first. If PeriodicEndCorrection is true, then it is assumed that the input data goes from 0-1 (or whatever scaled/shifted actual time) and time 1 is the same as time 0 so that steps will be 0,1,2,3...N,1,2,3...N,1,2,3 where step N is the same as 0 and step 0 is not repeated. When this flag is false the data is assumed to be literal and output is of the form 0,1,2,3...N,0,1,2,3... By default this flag is ON | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PostShift` | The amount of time the input is shifted. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `PreShift` | Apply a translation to the data before scaling. To convert T{5,100} to T{0,1} use Preshift=-5, Scale=1/95, PostShift=0 To convert T{5,105} to T{5,10} use Preshift=-5, Scale=5/100, PostShift=5 | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Scale` | The factor by which the input time is scaled. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
